articles.title: First time buyers shun leasehold flats – data
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of landlords are thought to be trying to sell their flats
articles.ai_summary:

- Thousands of landlords are now faced with selling their properties as demand declines.

articles.title: New Tory housing chief’s blistering attack on Renters Right Act
articles.summary: The new shadow housing secretary has started with a blistering attack on the department she one day hopes to run. In an article on the Conservative Home website, Katie Lam gives a withering analysis of the government’s policies enacted by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. Four quotes from the article give an […]
articles.ai_summary:
- New Tory housing chief Katie Lam criticizes the government's Renters Right Act, expressing strong opposition to current housing policies.
- Lam’s attack indicates a broader strategy to reshape housing discussions within the Conservative party as she prepares for future leadership.

articles.title: Most tenants completely unaware about guarantor services
articles.summary: Over 700 landlords and 850 tenants have been surveyed
articles.ai_summary:
- A recent survey of over 700 landlords and 850 tenants reveals that most tenants are oblivious to the existence of guarantor services.  
- This lack of awareness highlights a potential opportunity for property managers and landlords to educate renters on the benefits and availability of guarantor options.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act creates massive extra red tape
articles.summary: A survey of some 550 lettings professionals has produced this unsurprising result
articles.ai_summary:
- A recent survey reveals that 550 lettings professionals view the Renters Rights Act as imposing significant additional regulatory burdens.  
- Industry experts are expressing concerns about the complexities and challenges the Act presents to property management.

articles.title: Council boasts of forcing landlord to pay thousands to tenant
articles.summary: The Rent Repayment Order followed an investigation by a council
articles.ai_summary:
- A council successfully secured a Rent Repayment Order, compelling a landlord to pay thousands to a tenant.
- The ruling highlights the council's effective investigation into landlord misconduct.

articles.title: Lender cuts Buy To Let rates to woo landlords
articles.ai_summary:
- Lenders are slashing Buy To Let rates to attract more landlords to the market.  
- The new rates are effective immediately, offering potential savings for property investors.

articles.title: Trusted builder scheme aims to protect landlords from cowboys
articles.summary: It's the latest of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's attempts to help people
articles.ai_summary:
- Prime Minister Andy Burnham introduces a trusted builder scheme to safeguard landlords against unscrupulous contractors.

articles.title: Rent tribunal cases surge as tenants grab power
articles.ai_summary:
- Rent Repayment Orders are on the rise in the UK, reflecting increased tenant empowerment in disputes with landlords.  
- A notable surge in rent tribunal cases signals a shift in the balance of power towards tenants seeking justice.

articles.title: Crisis as HMRC data shows landlord expenses soaring

articles.ai_summary:
- Landlord expenses are skyrocketing, according to recent HMRC data analyzed by a lettings agency, signalling a potential crisis in the rental market.  
- Increased costs threaten rental yields, prompting concerns about the viability of property investment for landlords.

articles.title: Married landlords harassed and illegally evicted tenant
articles.summary: The rogue landlords operated in south London
articles.ai_summary:
- A married couple in south London faced legal action for harassing and illegally evicting their tenant.

articles.title: HMO landlords invest thousands despite red tape and tax
articles.summary: Over a quarter of landlords expect to pay a five figure sum this year
articles.ai_summary:

- Many landlords anticipate spending a five-figure sum, highlighting their commitment to the market despite challenges.

articles.title: Young new MP becomes Tory shadow housing secretary
articles.summary: A 35 year old MP elected for the first time in 2024 has been appointed as the shadow housing secretary – the Tories’ pick facing Angela Rayner. Katie Lam replaces Sir James Cleverly, the experienced former Cabinet minister who is now to contest the London Mayoral election in 2027. While studying at Cambridge University she […]
articles.ai_summary:
- 35-year-old Katie Lam steps up as the Tory shadow housing secretary, taking on Angela Rayner in a key political role after her first election win in 2024.  
- Lam succeeds Sir James Cleverly, who shifts focus to the 2027 London Mayoral election after his tenure in housing.
